description: Helpers at The Lord of the Rings: assistance with registration, the children’s game, weapon checks, camp logistics or clean-up. What to expect, what reward is possible, and how to sign up.
title: Helpers
subtitle: Without you the camp wouldn’t stand. Without us, neither.
who_p1: Helpers are participants who want to help with organisation, preparation, the programme or camp logistics. You can help short-term, for the whole weekend, or only during a specific phase of the event.
who_p2_pre: At the same time, a helper does not have to miss out on the experience. Help happens
who_p2_post: and can be set up so that you can still enjoy The Lord of the Rings as a regular participant.
who_p3: A helper might be someone who:
who_l1: is coming to the event for the first time and wants to get involved,
who_l2: doesn’t want to fight but wants to be useful,
who_l3: wants to play normally and also help with a specific part of the programme,
who_l5: wants to support their army or the whole camp,
who_l6: wants to get close to the organising team and gradually do more.
h_60s: The most important things in 60 seconds
s60_l1: A helper is not automatically an organiser.
s60_l2: You only help according to what was agreed, your time and your possibilities.
s60_l3: You can still enjoy the event as a regular participant.
s60_l4: You can help with registration, the programme, logistics, the children’s game, clean-up or camp logistics.
s60_l5: If you commit to something, we count on you.
s60_l6: Depending on how much you contribute, we may reward you with a discount, a fee waiver or covered food and drink.
s60_l7: If you’re not sure, ask first rather than improvising in a sensitive situation.
what1_p: Helping with checking in participants, paperwork, parking cards and orientation for new arrivals. Suitable for patient people who can communicate well and keep order even when many people arrive at once.
what2_p: Helping with the programme for young adventurers. Suitable for people who like children, are patient and can keep an eye on safety as well as atmosphere. May involve activity stations, games, crafts, side activities or simple logistics.
what3_p: Helping with arenas, the market, micro-quests, capture-the-flag, small games or side programme. Friday is the perfect space for camp life and smaller in-game activities.
what4_p: Helping with water, firewood, small repairs, waste, orientation for visitors, area checks, signage or coordination with the pub. These aren’t the most visible roles, but often the most important.
what5_p: Helping with line-up, instructions, movement, organising space or playing NPCs. During the main game it is essential to follow the instructions of responsible organisers and not to improvise where it could affect safety or the course of play.
what6_p: Packing, cleaning the campsite, checking the area after the event and helping leave the place tidy. Sunday is not the in-game finale — it’s the day we clean up after ourselves and say goodbye.
h_engagement: How much do you have to commit?
eng_intro: Help is always by agreement. You can help:
eng_l5: or get involved more substantially across the whole weekend.
eng_note: The goal isn’t to “lock you into work”. The goal is to find a balance between what the event needs and what you want to enjoy.
reward_intro: Depending on how much you help, we may agree on a reward, for example:
reward_l1: a discount on the registration fee,
reward_l2: a full waiver of the registration fee,
reward_l4: an individual arrangement based on the scope of your help.
reward_alert: It is not automatic for every helper. It always depends on scope, type of help and prior agreement.
h_from_us: What you can expect from us
from_us_l1: A specific assignment based on what you enjoy and what you’re good at.
from_us_l2: A short briefing before each activity.
from_us_l3: A clear contact person whenever possible.
from_us_l4: Space for your own initiative where it is safe and useful.
from_us_l5: A fair agreement on the scope of help and any reward.
from_us_l6: Respect and gratitude. Helpers are not invisible.
from_you_l1: Reliability — if we agree on a time and task, we count on you.
from_you_l2: A calm head even in more demanding moments.
from_you_l3: A willingness to handle things politely.
from_you_l4: The ability to say “I don’t know, I’ll ask”.
from_you_l5: Respect for the community and gratitude.
from_you_l6: Teamwork with other helpers and organisers.
reg_p1: Helpers register according to the agreed role and scope of help. For some helpers an individual arrangement on the registration fee may be possible — discount, fee waiver or covered food and drink. It is not automatic; it is decided based on the scope of help and the needs of the event.
reg_p2: You will receive payment information immediately after registration. You can pay by QR code or bank transfer. If you’re negotiating an individual arrangement, write to us first.
